routines.semantics: Write the closure of the input window’s complement relative to the closed interval [left,right]. Clip at the bounds, retain closure endpoints and replace the caller-owned destination, which must be distinct from the input.

An empty input leaves the whole bounding interval.

A covered bounding interval needs no result endpoints and uses a logical zero-capacity cell.
A one-interval destination cannot hold all complement intervals. Observe the actual toolkit error WINDOWEXCESS.
The left complement bound exceeds the right bound. Observe the actual toolkit error BADENDPOINTS.

routines.errorAssessment: Reversed bounds raise SPICE(BADENDPOINTS). Insufficient result capacity raises SPICE(WINDOWEXCESS). Opaque handle ownership and invalid storage are checked independently at the wrapper boundary.
routines.fixtureRationale: Authored numeric endpoints and capacities create real windows in both implementations. No kernels, external files or datasets are required.
routines.cleanup: The caller owns each input and result handle. Case-scoped finalizers free allocated windows. Node holds the shared lock during native handle resolution and the call. WASM validates module ownership and releases per-call temporaries on success or error. A failed C wrapper can leave the C descriptor unsynchronized with the underlying window control block. The shim validates the physical written endpoint count before window reads and clears preservation after an explicit cardinality reset. The output must be distinct from all inputs. Toolkit errors are captured and reset. Failure may leave a partially written result.
routines.tolerance: Interval counts, indices, selector/relation results and expected errors compare exactly. Finite endpoint/measure outputs use the unchanged live comparison (1e−12 absolute or relative). The workflow reads every resulting interval in order.

routines.semantics: Write the union of A and B into the distinct caller-owned result. The pinned merge has capacity-dependent behavior when the result is already full. With [0,4] and [2,8], capacities of zero, one and two intervals return empty, [0,4] and [0,8], respectively. Registered cases preserve this actual output together with ordinary touching/overlapping and identical inputs.

scenarios.observes: Evaluate both operand orders, overwriting the same result, and retain each input endpoint.
Touching boundaries and isolated points distinguish closed interval algebra.
Read empty input in either operand position and overwrite a previously nonempty result.
Input operands may share a live handle; the destination remains independently allocated.
Compare a contained interval and a distant disjoint interval against both operand orders.
The explicit one-interval destination cannot hold this result. Observe the actual toolkit error WINDOWEXCESS.
Two disjoint intervals exactly fill the caller-owned result.
N0067 extends only a local endpoint once storage is full. Observe the same overlapping union at capacities one, two and zero.

routines.edgeAssessment: Read all intervals after reversing operands, identical handles, empty/nested/disjoint/touching and singleton combinations. Compare exact- and insufficient-capacity destinations.
routines.errorAssessment: Disjoint intervals can exceed the destination capacity and raise SPICE(WINDOWEXCESS). Opaque handle ownership and invalid storage are checked independently at the wrapper boundary.
routines.fixtureRationale: Authored numeric endpoints and capacities create real windows in both implementations. No kernels, external files or datasets are required.
routines.cleanup: The caller owns each input and result handle. Case-scoped finalizers free allocated windows. Node holds the shared lock during native handle resolution and the call. WASM validates module ownership and releases per-call temporaries on success or error. A failed C wrapper can leave the C descriptor unsynchronized with the underlying window control block. The shim validates the physical written endpoint count before window reads and clears preservation after an explicit cardinality reset. The output must be distinct from all inputs. Toolkit errors are captured and reset. Failure may leave a partially written result.
routines.tolerance: Interval counts, indices, selector/relation results and expected errors compare exactly. Finite endpoint/measure outputs use the unchanged live comparison (1e−12 absolute or relative). The workflow reads every resulting interval in order.

findings.summary: The installed high-level SpiceyPy wrapper creates its own output window. That representation loses the caller’s capacity and existing contents, including observable state after a failed write.
findings.repair: Use the exact typed canonical symbol in a separate ctypes function table, passing distinct already-allocated input and result SpiceCells. Check the toolkit error status after the call. Compare destination replacement, capacity and the canonical window reads.

findings.summary: When the result storage is exactly full, the pinned WNUNID routine tracks a later overlapping endpoint in its local END without updating the last stored interval. A call can succeed with a capacity-dependent interval.
findings.repair: Preserve the actual result in caller-owned storage and exercise zero, one and two interval capacities explicitly. Document the pinned toolkit limitation without changing capacity or computing a replacement union.
